title: Configuring the NVMe-oF gateway target
content:
Use `ceph nvmeof` commands to configure targets, LUNs, and clients.

Before configuring the NVMe-oF gateway target, verify that the following services are installed and running on the storage system:

- IBM Storage Ceph 9.9.0 or later cluster
- Ceph NVMe-oF gateway
- IBM Storage Ceph Dashboard 9.9.0 or later
section_path: Configuring the NVMe-oF gateway target

title: Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem
content: Define an NVMe-oF subsystem. Defining the NVMe subsystem includes creating an NVMe subsystem, configuring the IP port for communication, and enabling hosts to use the subsystem.
section_path: Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem

title: Before you begin
content:
**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 To use the ceph nvmeof commands, the latest Ceph Dashboard must be installed. If the Ceph Dashboard is not available, go to Using the nvmeof-cli utility for configuring and managing NVMe-oF gateways.

Before you begin, make sure that you have the following prerequisites in place:

- The latest Ceph Dashboard installed. For more information, see Bootstrap storage cluster along with Dashboard .
- To use in-band authentication, an RSA encryption key must be created and placed in the specification file.
 
For more information, see Deploying by using a service specification file.
- Generate a DH-HMAC-CHAP key with the Linux command line.
 
**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 In-band authentication is supported on an initiator with Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.5 or later. ESX is not supported.

This is required for using both bidirectional and unidirectional in-band authentication.
 
```bash
nvme gen-dhchap-key
```

For example,
 
```
$ nvme gen-dhchap-key
DHHC-1:00:abEcb12F100FNlZkIOkv37idpu/notvalid!!si1VQ09KhKv2g:
```

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 This prerequisite is only required if defining in-band authentication during the subsystem creation or while adding a host to a subsystem. The in-band authentication can also be defined later.

- For more information about in-band authentication, see NVMe-oF gateway in-band authentication.
- For more information about adding in-band authentication to a subsystem after creation, see Changing a subsystem authentication key.
section_path: Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem > Before you begin

title: About this task
content:
Use this procedure to configure the Ceph NVMe-oF gateway with the command-line interface. To configure the gateway with the dashboard, see Managing NVMe-oF subsystems.

When creating a subsystem, you can optionally configure NVMe‑oF listeners automatically. Automatic listeners are created on all gateways whose IP addresses fall within the specified network subnet. To enable automatic listener creation, use the --network-mask parameter with the subsystem add command.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Configure NVMe‑oF listeners automatically by using the --network-mask parameter. This approach simplifies listener management and ensures that listeners are automatically added or removed during scale‑up and scale‑down operations.
section_path: Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem > About this task

title: Procedure
content:
1. Create an NVMe subsystem.
The NQN is a required parameter when creating a subsystem. NQN is a user-defined string. By default, the gateway appends a group name to the NQN and the subsystem includes the group name. The group name is automatically appended to prevent one or more subsystems from being created with the same NQN in different groups.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 A group name is not appended if the --no-group-append parameter is used when adding the subsystem.

In this example, NQN is defined as nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1 and `group1` is appended after the subsystem add command.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:

- The actual created subsystem name is returned with the subsystem add command. Use the returned subsystem name for all subsequent subsystem operations.
- Up to 128 subsystems are supported.

```bash
ceph nvmeof subsystem add --nqn NQN [--enable-ha] [--network-mask IP_SUBNET] [--max_namespaces MAX_NAMESPACES ] [--no-group-append] [--serial_number SERIAL_NUMBER ] [--dhchap-key KEY_VALUE]
```

**Important:** **Note:** Important:

- NQN and gateway name values must not contain an underscore character.
- Do not use the same NQN for two different gateway groups. Namespaces might not be visible if an initiator is connected to two different gateway groups with the same NQN.

For extra input, the following parameters can be added to the command:
 
--enable-ha
Use to enable High Availability (HA), if HA was previously not enabled. For more information, see Ceph NVMe-oF gateway .
--network-mask
Use to enable automatic listener creation.
 When you specify a network mask:
 
- Listeners are created automatically on all gateways with IP addresses within the subnet.
- Listeners are automatically added when gateways are scaled up.
- Listeners are automatically removed when gateways are scaled down.
- Manual creation of listeners is not required.

--max-namespaces
The maximum namespaces per subsystem default is 256.
 
Input type: Number

 --no-group-append
Use this flag to not append a group name to the subsystem NQN.
 
**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 Use this flag with extreme caution. When using this flag, if an initiator is connected to two different gateway groups with the same subsystem NQNs, not all NVMe-oF devices are listed with the nvme list command.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 A group name is not appended to the subsystem NQN only if this option is not used.

Input type: Boolean

--serial-number
If the serial number is not specified, the number is randomly generated.
 
Input type: String

--dhchap-key
Use this flag to add a generated DH-HMAC-CHAP key for use with bidirectional in-band authentication.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Use this flag to define in-band authentication during the subsystem creation. The in-band authentication can also be defined later. For more information, see Changing a subsystem authentication key.

Input type: String

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# ceph nvmeof subsystem add --nqn nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1 --network-mask 10.243.64.0/24 --dhchap-key DHHC-1:00:abEcb12F100FNlZkIOkv37idpu/notvalid!!si1VQ09KhKv2g:
Success
```
2. Add a listener to define the IP port on the gateway that is to process NVMe/TCP commands and I/O operations.

**Important:** **Note:** Important:

- Listeners must be added to all subsystems for all gateways in the gateway group for High Availability and auto load balancing of namespaces.
- NQN and gateway name values must not contain an underscore character.
- If a subsystem is already enabled with auto-listeners, do not manually add a listener.

```bash
ceph nvmeof listener add --nqn NQN --host-name HOST_NAME [--traddr LISTENER_ADDRESS] [--server-address SERVER_ADDRESS] [--trsvcid:int PORT] [--adrfam:int IPV_TYPE] [--gw_group GW_GROUP]
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# ceph nvmeof listener add --nqn nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --host-name host02 --server-address 10.172.19.01 --trsvcid:int 5500 --adrfam:int 0 --gw_group GW_GROUP
Success
```
section_path: Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem > Procedure (part 1)

title: Procedure
content:
For extra input, the following flags can optionally be added to the command:

- TRADDR
- TRSVCID

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 To define the IP port on the gateway, be sure to include the TRSVCID:INT information.
- ADRFAM:INT
- GW_GROUP
3. Get the host NVMe Qualified Name (NQN) for each host.

For Red Hat Enterprise Linux initiators

```bash
cat /etc/nvme/hostnqn
```

 For example,
 
```
# cat /etc/nvme/hostnqn
nqn.2014-08.org.nvmexpress:uuid:950ddadf-f995-47b7-9416-b9bb233f66e3
```

 In this example `950ddadf-f995-47b7-9416-b9bb233f66e3` is the UUID. 
For VMware ESXi initiators

```bash
esxcli nvme info get
```

 For example,
 
```
esxcli nvme info get
Host NQN: nqn.2014-08.com.ibm.ceph:nvme:host01
```
4. Allow the NVMe initiator host to run NVMe/TCP commands to the newly created NVMe subsystem.

1. Add the host.

**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 To add a secured DH-HMAC-CHAP host, use the --dhchap-key parameter to add the DHCHAP_KEY to the host.
 
`--host-nqn "*"` is not supported with DH-HMAC-CHAP host.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 A specific host can be selected, as in the following example. To specify all hosts, use `--host-nqn "*"`.
 
To add multiple specific hosts, separate them by using a space. Do not use commas between host NQNs or quotes (") around the multiple host NQNs. Use the following example format:

--host-nqn HOST01_NQN HOST02_NQN

```bash
ceph nvmeof host add --nqn NQN [--host_nqn HOST_NQN] [--dhchap_key KEY_VALUE] [--psk PSK] [--gw_group GW_GROUP] [--server-address SERVER_ADDRESS]
```

```
Success
```

2. Verify the hosts defined on the subsystem.

```bash

```

- Use the --clear-alerts parameter to clear host alert signals after retrieving the values.
- Use the optional --gw_group and --server-address to specify specific gateway group, gateway IP address, or both in the host list.

For example,
 
```

[root@host01 ~]#
```
5. Verify by listing all NVMe-oF gateway target entities configured on the gateway.

1. List the subsystems.

```bash
ceph nvmeof subsystem list [--gw_group GW_GROUP] [--server-address SERVER_ADDRESS]
```

title: Defining block devices to use NVMe/TCP
content: Define storage block devices to be used with NVMe/TCP by using `ceph nvmeof` commands.

title: About this task
content:
**Note:** **Note:** Note:

title: Procedure
content:
To define block devices and add namespaces on existing rbd images in a Ceph cluster, start directly with step 3.
1. Create an `rbd` pool.

```bash
ceph osd pool create POOL_NAME PG_NUM
 
ceph osd pool application enable POOL_NAME rbd
rbd pool init -p POOL_NAME
```

For example,
 
```
[root@rbd-client ~]# ceph osd pool create pool1
[root@rbd-client ~]# ceph osd pool application enable pool1 rbd
[root@rbd-client ~]# rbd pool init -p pool1
```
2. **Optional: **
Create an image within any Ceph Block Device (RBD) application-enabled pool.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 An image can be created separately, by using this step, or while adding a namespace. To create an image directly during the namespace creation, skip this step and go to step 3. Be sure to add the --rbd-create-image and --size parameters.

```bash
rbd create IMAGE_NAME --size=MEGABYTES --pool=POOL_NAME
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# rbd create image1 --size=1024 --pool=pool1
```

For more information about creating an image, see Creating images.
3. Add a namespace to any subsystem that was created in Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem.
To create an image within an RBD application-enabled pool, use the --rbd-create-image and --size parameters.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Create an image within an RBD application-enabled pool when step 2 was skipped.

Automatic load-balancing makes sure that each namespace receives an assigned load-balancing group. For more information about load balancing, see Using load balancing with scale-up and scale-down.

During a namespace addition, a load-balancing group is automatically assigned to the NVMe-oF namespace with any available NVMe-oF gateway load-balancing group.

It is recommended to allow the NVMe-oF gateway to set the active gateway automatically, and not to force the namespace. The gateway load-balancing group ID of a gateway can be retrieved at any time by running the gateway info command. For example:
 
```bash
ceph nvmeof gateway info [--gw_group GW_GROUP]
```

```bash
ceph nvmeof namespace add --nqn NQN [--rbd_image_name RBD_IMAGE_NAME] [--rbd_pool RBD_POOL] [--create-image] [--size POOL_SIZE] [--rbd_image_size IMAGE_SIZE]
```

The image size can be expanded at any time. For more information see, Expanding a block device image.

- Example of adding a namespace to a block device with a previously created image.
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# ceph nvmeof namespace add nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 rbd_image_name image1 --rbd_pool pool1
```
- Example of creating an image and adding a namespace within the same command.
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# ceph nvmeof namespace add nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --rbd_image_name image1 pool1 --create-image --size SIZE --rbd_image_size 1024
```

title: Configuring the NVMe-oF gateway initiator
content:
Configure the initiator to allow the NVMe/TCP protocol to send NVMe-oF commands to targets over an Internet Protocol network.

The NVMe-oF gateway initiator can be configured on either of the following platform version:
 
- Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.2 or later
- VMware vSphere Hypervisor (ESXi) 7.0U3 or later

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 The NVMe reserve command is supported.
section_path: Configuring the NVMe-oF gateway initiator

title: Configuring the NVMe-oF initiator for Red Hat Enterprise Linux
content: Configure the NVMe-oF initiator for Red Hat Enterprise Linux.
section_path: Configuring the NVMe-oF initiator for Red Hat Enterprise Linux

title: Before you begin
content: Before you begin, make sure that you have Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.2 or later.
section_path: Configuring the NVMe-oF initiator for Red Hat Enterprise Linux > Before you begin

title: Procedure
content:
1. Install the `nvme-cli`.

```bash
yum install nvme-cli
```
2. Load the `nvme-fabrics` module using `modprobe`.

```bash
modprobe nvme-fabrics
```
3. Verify that the target is reachable from the initiator.

```bash
nvme discover -t tcp -a GATEWAY_IP -s 8009
```

The output provides the IP address of the NVMe-oF subsystems that can be connected from this initiator.

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvme discover --transport tcp -a 10.172.19.01 -s 8009
=====Discovery Log Entry 0======
trtype: tcp
adrfam: ipv4
subtype: nvme subsystem
treq: not required
portid: 0
trsvcid: 4420
subnqn: nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1
traddr: 9.147.168.14
eflags: none
sectype: none
=====Discovery Log Entry 1======
trtype: tcp
adrfam: ipv4
subtype: nvme subsystem
treq: not required
portid: 1
trsvcid: 4420
subnqn: nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1
traddr: 9.147.168.32
eflags: none
sectype: none
```
4. Connect to the NVMe-oF target.

Use either the nvme connect-all or nvme connect command to connect to all gateways in the group, establishing multipath connections.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 When using bidirectional in-band authentication, use the nvme connect command instead of nvme connect-all. The nvme connect command must be run on each gateway for all namespaces to be visible with DH-HMAC-CHAP keys.

**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 Namespaces might not be visible if an initiator is connected to two different gateway groups with the same NQN.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Adding the `-l` flag enables the initiator to retry connecting to the gateway in cases where the gateway becomes temporarily unavailable.

- Running the nvme connect-all command.
 
```bash
nvme connect-all --traddr GATEWAY_IP --transport tcp -l 1800 -s 8009
```
- Running the nvme connect command, to connect to a specific subsystem.
 
```bash
nvme connect --traddr GATEWAY_IP --transport tcp --nqn SUBSYSTEM_NQN --trsvcid PORT
```

Use the following values from the previous step:
 
- subnqn value as the SUBSYSTEM_NQN
- The trsvcid port value
- Running the nvme connect command, when bidirectional in-band authentication is enabled.
 The command runs all initiators for all gateway IPs for High Availability and auto load balancing.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Run this command again after a gateway is scaled up in a gateway group to the new gateways.

```bash
nvme connect --traddr GATEWAY_IP --transport tcp --nqn SUBSYSTEM_NQN --trsvcid PORT --dhchap-secret KEY_VALUE --dhchap-ctrl-secret KEY_VALUE
```
- Running the nvme connect-all command, when unidirectional in-band authentication is enabled.
 
```bash
nvme connect-all --traddr GATEWAY_IP --transport tcp --nqn SUBSYSTEM_NQN --trsvcid PORT --dhchap-secret KEY_VALUE
```

```
Allocating group tables: done
Writing inode tables: done
Writing superblocks and filesystem accounting information: done
```

4. Mount the NVMe node on the NVMe-oF directory.
 
1. Mount NVMe-oF.
 
```bash
mkdir /mnt/nvmeof
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# mkdir /mnt/nvmeof
```

2. Mount the node on within the NVMe-oF directory.
 
```bash
mount NVME_NODE_PATH /mnt/nvmeof
```

For example,

```
[root@host01 ~]# mount /home/nvme01_node01 /mnt/nvmeof
```

```bash
ls /mnt/nvmeof
```

For example,
 
```

```
6. Create a text file within the mnt/nvmeof directory.
 For example,
 
```
$ sudo bash -c "echo Hello NVMe-oF > /mnt/nvmeof/hello.txt"
```
7. Verify that the text file can now be reached.
 For example,
 
```
$ cat /mnt/nvmeof/hello.txt

```

title: Configuring the NVMe-oF initiator for VMware ESXi
content: Configure the NVMe-oF initiator for VMware vSphere Hypervisor (ESXi). You can set up a VMware ESXi host as a NVMe/TCP initiator.
section_path: Configuring the NVMe-oF initiator for VMware ESXi

title: Before you begin
content:
- A VMware ESXi host that is running VMware vSphere Hypervisor (ESXi) 7.0U3 version or later.
- Ceph NVMe-oF gateway deployed.
- IBM Storage Ceph cluster and `ceph-nvmeof` configurations are ready and working correctly.
- A subsystem defined within the gateway. For more information, see Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem with nvmeof-cli.
- NVMe/TCP adapter is configured.
 
- Enabled NVMe/TCP on a physical network interface controller (NIC).
 
```bash
esxcli nvme fabrics enable --protocol TCP --device vmnicN
```

 Replace N with the number of NIC.
- Tag a VMkernel NIC to allow NVMe/TCP traffic.
 
```bash
esxcli network ip interface tag add --interface-name vmkN --tagname NVMeTCP
```

 Replace N with the ID of the VMkernel.

title: Enabling and disabling NVMe-oF gateways
content: Temporarily disable or enable NVMe-oF gateways for maintenance and controlled failover scenarios.
section_path: Enabling and disabling NVMe-oF gateways

title: About this task
content:
NVMe-oF gateways can be administratively disabled to support maintenance or controlled failover scenarios. To perform maintenance on a gateway, disable it to stop servicing I/O and re-enable it after the maintenance is complete.

When a gateway is disabled, I/O traffic is redirected to other available gateways in the group. Re-enabling the gateway allows it to resume normal operation.
section_path: Enabling and disabling NVMe-oF gateways > About this task

title: Procedure
content:
1. Disable an NVMe-oF gateway.

```bash
ceph nvme-gw disable GW_ID NVME-OF_POOL_NAME NVME-OF_GROUP_NAME
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# ceph nvme-gw disable nvmeof_pool01.nvmeof_group01 .nvme.rbd group1
```

The gateway stops servicing I/O, and traffic is redirected to other gateways.
2. Enable the NVMe-oF gateway.
After maintenance or troubleshooting activities are complete and the gateway is verified to be healthy, re-enable the gateway to restore normal I/O processing.
 
```bash
ceph nvme-gw enable GW_ID NVME-OF_POOL_NAME NVME-OF_GROUP_NAME
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# ceph nvme-gw enable nvmeof_pool01.nvmeof_group01 .nvme.rbd group1
```

The gateway resumes servicing I/O and normal traffic distribution.

title: Monitoring NVMe-oF performance with ceph nvmeof top
content:
Monitor real-time CPU utilization and I/O performance for NVMe-oF gateways, subsystems, and namespaces.

The `ceph nvmeof top` commands provide a top-style, refresh-based view of NVMe-oF gateway performance. Use these commands to observe CPU usage on gateway nodes and I/O activity at the subsystem and namespace level.

The following are the current available ceph nvmeof top commands to use for monitoring.

`ceph nvmeof top cpu`
Monitors CPU utilization for NVMe-oF gateway threads. For more information, see Monitoring gateway CPU utilization.
`ceph nvmeof top io`
Monitors I/O performance for namespaces within an NVMe-oF subsystem. For more information, see Monitoring subsystem and namespace I/O performance.
section_path: Monitoring NVMe-oF performance with ceph nvmeof top

title: Monitoring gateway CPU utilization
content:
Use the `ceph nvmeof top cpu` command to monitor CPU usage across NVMe-oF gateway nodes. By default, the command displays CPU statistics for all gateways in the service. Table 1 details the different available syntax options.

```bash
ceph nvmeof top cpu [--server-address ADDRESS]
 [--server-port PORT]
 [--gw-group GROUP]
 [--sort-by COLUMN]
 [--descending]
 [--period SECONDS]
 [--with-timestamp]
 [--no-header]
```

| Parameter | Value | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------------------ | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| --server-address | IP address | All gateways | Limits the output to CPU statistics reported by a single NVMe-oF gateway. If not specified, CPU statistics are shown for all gateways in the service. |
| --server-port | Port number | 5500 | Specifies the management port used to communicate with the NVMe-oF gateway. |
| --gw-group | Gateway group name | Current group | Specifies the gateway group to monitor. This parameter is required when multiple NVMe-oF gateway groups exist. |
| --sort-by | Column name | Thread name | Sorts the output by the specified column. Valid values correspond to the output column headers, such as Busy rate (%) or Idle rate (%). |
| --descending | Flag - none | Ascending order | Sorts the output in descending order based on the selected sort-by column. |
| --period | Seconds (1–3600) | 1 | Specifies the refresh interval, in seconds, between successive samples of CPU statistics. |
| --with-timestamp | Flag - none | Disabled | Prefixes each refresh of the output with a timestamp and the elapsed time since the previous sample. |
| --no-header | Flag - none | Headers shown | Suppresses the column headers in the output. This option is useful when the output is redirected to a file or processed by scripts. |

The following is an example output. Table 2 describes avalable the output fields.
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# ceph nvmeof top cpu
Gateway Thread Name Busy Rate% Idle Rate% 
10.243.64.210:5500 app_thread 100.00 100.00 
10.243.64.209:5500 app_thread 100.00 100.00 
10.243.64.210:5500 nvmf_tgt_poll_group_000 100.00 100.00 
10.243.64.209:5500 nvmf_tgt_poll_group_000 100.00 100.00 
10.243.64.210:5500 nvmf_tgt_poll_group_001 100.00 100.00 
10.243.64.209:5500 nvmf_tgt_poll_group_001 100.00 100.00 
10.243.64.210:5500 nvmf_tgt_poll_group_002 100.00 100.00 
10.243.64.209:5500 nvmf_tgt_poll_group_002 100.00 100.00 
10.243.64.210:5500 nvmf_tgt_poll_group_003 100.00 100.00 
10.243.64.209:5500 nvmf_tgt_poll_group_003 100.00 100.00
```

| Field | Description |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gateway | Gateway IP address and management port. |
| Thread name | Name of the NVMe-oF or SPDK thread running on the gateway. |
| Busy rate (%) | Percentage of time the thread is busy. |
| Idle rate (%) | Percentage of time the thread is idle. |
section_path: Monitoring NVMe-oF performance with ceph nvmeof top > Monitoring gateway CPU utilization

title: Monitoring subsystem and namespace I/O performance
content:
Use the `ceph nvmeof top io` command to monitor I/O statistics for namespaces within an NVMe-oF subsystem. The subsystem NQN is required. Table 3 details the different available syntax options.

```bash
ceph nvmeof top io --nqn SUBSYSTEM_NQN
 [--server-address ADDRESS]
 [--server-port PORT]
 [--gw-group GROUP]
 [--sort-by COLUMN]
 [-descending]
 [--summary]
 [--period SECONDS]
 [--with-timestamp]
 [--no-header]
```

| Parameter | Value | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------------------ | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| --nqn | Subsystem NQN | None | Specifies the NVMe-oF subsystem for which namespace I/O statistics are displayed. This parameter is required. |
| --server-address | IP address | All gateways | Limits the output to namespaces optimized on the specified NVMe-oF gateway. If not specified, namespace statistics are aggregated across gateways. |
| --server-port | Port number | 5500 | Specifies the management port used to communicate with the NVMe-oF gateway. |
| --gw-group | Gateway group name | Current group | Specifies the gateway group that hosts the subsystem. This parameter is required when multiple NVMe-oF gateway groups exist. |
| --sort-by | Column name | NSID | Sorts the output by the specified column. Valid values correspond to the output column headers, such as IOPS or rMB/s. |
| --descending | Flag - none | Ascending order | Sorts the output in descending order based on the selected sort-by column. |
| --summary | Flag - none | Disabled | Displays aggregated I/O statistics for the subsystem. When combined with a server address, the output reflects gateway- level aggregation. |
| --period | Seconds (1–3600) | 1 | Specifies the refresh interval, in seconds, between successive samples of namespace I/O statistics. |
| --with-timestamp | Flag - none | Disabled | Prefixes each refresh of the output with a timestamp and the elapsed time since the previous sample. |
| --no-header | Flag - none | Headers shown | Suppresses the column headers in the output. This option is useful when the output is redirected to a file or processed by scripts. |

The following is an example output. Table 4 describes the available output fields.

```
[root@host01 ~]# ceph nvmeof top io --nqn nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.mygroup1

NSID RBD Image IOPS r/s rMB/s r_await rareq-sz w/s wMB/s w_await wareq-sz LBGrp QoS
 1 nvmeof/myimage1 61 61 0.72 0.65 12.17 0 0.00 0.00 0.00 1 No
 2 nvmeof/myimage2 61 61 0.72 0.67 12.17 0 0.00 0.00 0.00 2 No
 3 nvmeof/myimage3 61 61 0.72 0.53 12.17 0 0.00 0.00 0.00 1 No
```

| Field | Description |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| NSID | Namespace identifier within the subsystem. |
| RBD Image | Ceph Block Device image backing the namespace. |
| IOPS | Total input/output operations per second. |
| r/s, w/s | Read and write operations per second. |
| rMB/s, wMB/s | Read and write throughput in megabytes per second. |
| r_await, w_await | Average read and write latency. |
| rareq-sz, wareq-sz | Average size of read and write requests in KB. |
| LBGrp | Load-balancing group currently serving the namespace. |
| QoS | Indicates whether Quality of Service limits are applied. |

title: Managing NVMe-oF gateway host labels

title: Procedure
content:
1. Add a label to the host.

```bash
ceph orch host label add NODE LABEL
```

```
[ceph: root@host01 /]# ceph orch host label add host01 nvmeof_label
[ceph: root@host01 /]# ceph orch host label add host02 nvmeof_label
```

In this example, the NODE name is host01 and host02 and the LABEL is nvmeof_label.
2. Display the labels associated with the host.

```bash
ceph orch host ls
```

For example,
 
```
[ceph: root@host01 /]# ceph orch host ls
HOST ADDR LABELS STATUS
host01 mon,mgr,_admin,nvmeof_label
host02 mon,mgr,_admin,nvmeof_label
```

```bash
ceph orch apply nvmeof NVME-OF_POOL_NAME GW_GROUP --placement="label:LABEL"
```

```
[ceph: root@host01 /]# ceph orch apply nvmeof nvmeof_pool01 group2 --placement="label:nvmeof_label"
```

title: Removing the NVMe-oF service
content: Remove the NVMe-oF service if you no longer use the NVMe-oF gateway or before running a fresh installation.

title: Before you begin
content:
Verify that the volumes are stopped before the service is removed.
 When disconnecting from an VMware ESX initiator, use the esxcli nvme controller list command to get the NQN name, controller number, and adapter values for step 1. For example,
 
```
esxcli nvme controller list
Name Controller Number Adapter Transport Type Is Online
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ----------------- ------- -------------- ---------
nqn.2014-08.org.nvmexpress_8086_INTEL_SSDPE2KX010T7_____________________PHLF733300LH1P0GGN 256 vmhba2 PCIe true
nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode2#vmhba64#10.0.210.14:4420 282 vmhba64 TCP false
nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 #vmhba64#10.0.210.14:4420 278 vmhba64 TCP false
```
section_path: Removing the NVMe-oF service > Before you begin

title: About this task
content:
The following steps provide a high-level overview of the process for removing the NVMe-oF service:
 
1. Disconnect the gateway initiator.
2. Remove the gateway target.
3. Remove the NVMe-oF service.
section_path: Removing the NVMe-oF service > About this task

title: Procedure
content:
1. Disconnect the NVMe-oF initiator from NVMe-oF target.

Red Hat Enterprise Linux

```bash
nvme disconnect-all
```

VMware ESX initiator 

```bash
esxcli nvme fabrics disconnect -n CONTROLLER_NUMBER -a ADAPTER -s SUBSYSTEM_NQN
```

 Replace the CONTROLLER_NUMBER, NVME_TCP_ADAPTER, and SUBSYSTEM_NQN values with the values retrieved from the esxcli nvme controller list command. The SUBSYSTEM_NQN is listed as `Name` in the system output.
 For example,
 
```
esxcli nvme fabrics disconnect -n 282 -a vmhba64 -s nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode2.group1
```
2. Remove the NVMe-oF Gateway target for each subsystem.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Use the`--force` flag to delete subsystems that contain namespaces.

```bash
ceph nvmeof subsystem del --nqn NQN --force
```

For example,
 
```bash
[root@host01 ~]# ceph nvmeof subsystem del --nqn nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --force
```
3. Remove the NVMe-oF service.

1. On the Ceph admin node, remove the NVMe-oF service.

```bash
ceph orch rm nvmeof.NVME-OF_POOL_NAME.GW_GROUP
```

For example,
 
```
[ceph: root@host01 /]# ceph orch rm nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1
```
2. Check that the mon_allow_pool_delete parameter is set to `true`

```bash
ceph config set mon mon_allow_pool_delete true
```
3. On the Ceph admin node, remove the NVME-OF_POOL created to host NVMe-oF service.

```bash
ceph osd pool rm NVME-OF_POOL_NAME NVME-OF_POOL_NAME --yes-i-really-really-mean-it
```

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 The pool name (NVME-OF_POOL_NAME) must be used twice in the command to remove the pool.

For example,
 
```
[ceph: root@host01 /]# ceph osd pool rm nvmeof_pool01 nvmeof_pool01 --yes-i-really-really-mean-it
```
section_path: Removing the NVMe-oF service > Procedure

title: General nvmeof-cli parameters
content:
Use the following `nvmeof-cli` command parameters for more defined commands.
 
| Parameter | Description |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| --format | View the output for each of these commands in any of the following format options: text, json, yaml, plain, or python. If not specified, the default is text. |
| --output | Use one of the following CLI output methods: log, stdio. If not specified, the default is log. Use stdio if the CLI output needs to be redirected to a file or another program. |
| --server-address | Use to specify the server address. |
| --server-port | Use to specify the server port. |
| --verbose | Use to run the CLI in verbose mode, for extra messages to be displayed. |
| --client-key | Used with mTLS. Use to provide a path to the client key file. |
| --client-cert | Used with mTLS. Use to provide a path to the client certificate file. |
| --server-key | Used with mTLS. Use to provide a path to the server key file. |

title: Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem with nvmeof-cli
content: Define an NVMe-oF subsystem. Defining the NVMe subsystem includes creating an NVMe subsystem, configuring the IP port for communication, and enabling hosts to use the subsystem.
section_path: Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem with nvmeof-cli

title: Before you begin
content:
Before you begin, make sure that you have the following prerequisites in place:

- (Optional) You can download the `nvmeof-cli` container before first use.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 The gateway `nvmeof-cli` container automatically downloads during initial container use on the host.

To download the gateway `nvmeof-cli` container, use the following command:
 
```bash
podman pull cp.icr.io/cp/ibm-ceph/nvmeof-cli-rhel9:v9.9.1
```

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 These commands can be run on either `podman` or `docker`.
- To use in-band authentication, an RSA encryption key must be created and placed in the specification file.
 
For more information, see Deploying by using a service specification file.
- Generate a DH-HMAC-CHAP key with the Linux command line.
 
**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 In-band authentication is supported on an initiator with Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.5 or later. ESX is not supported.

This is required for using both bidirectional and unidirectional in-band authentication.
 
```bash
nvme gen-dhchap-key
```

For example,
 
```
$ nvme gen-dhchap-key
DHHC-1:00:abEcb12F100FNlZkIOkv37idpu/notvalid!!si1VQ09KhKv2g:
```

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 This prerequisite is only required if defining in-band authentication during the subsystem creation or while adding a host to a subsystem. The in-band authentication can also be defined later.

- For more information about in-band authentication, see NVMe-oF gateway in-band authentication.
- For more information about adding in-band authentication to a subsystem after creation, see Changing a subsystem authentication key.
section_path: Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem with nvmeof-cli > Before you begin

title: About this task
content: Configure the Ceph NVMe-oF gateway by using the gateway `nvmeof-cli` utility. To configure the gateway with the dashboard, see Managing NVMe-oF subsystems.
section_path: Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem with nvmeof-cli > About this task

title: Procedure
content:
1. **Optional: **
Define an `nvmeof-cli` alias.
This step is recommended but optional. Creating an alias enables streamlined commands.
 
**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 If an alias is not created, be sure to replace `podman run --rm <cp.icr.io/cp/ibm-ceph/>` at the beginning of each command, instead of `nvmeof-cli`.

1. From the Linux command line, create the alias.

```bash
alias nvmeof-cli="podman run --rm cp.icr.io/cp/ibm-ceph/nvmeof-cli-rhel9:v9.9.1"
```

 By default the command line output goes to a logging facility, which is displayed to the console. To change the output placement, use the --output parameter. For example, --output stdio directs the output to stdout for informational messages and to stderr for error messages.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Changing the output placement to stdio, enables CLI calls to integrate more seamlessly into scripts and automation.
2. Verify that the alias is successfully created.

```bash
nvmeof-cli
```

When created successfully, the `nvmeof-cli` help menu is displayed.

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# alias nvmeof-cli="podman run --rm cp.icr.io/cp/ibm-ceph/nvmeof-cli-rhel9:v9.9.1"
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli
usage: python3 -m control.cli [-h] [--format {text,json,yaml,plain,python}]
 [--output {log,stdio}]
 [--log-level {debug,DEBUG,info,INFO,warning,WARNING,error,ERROR,critical,CRITICAL}]
 [--server-address SERVER_ADDRESS]
 [--server-port SERVER_PORT]
 [--client-key CLIENT_KEY]
 [--client-cert CLIENT_CERT]
 [--server-cert SERVER_CERT] [--verbose]
 {version,gw,spdk_log_level,subsystem,listener,host,connection,namespace,ns,get_subsystems}
 ...
CLI to manage NVMe gateways
optional arguments:
 -h, --help show this help message and exit
 --format {text,json,yaml,plain,python}
 CLI output format
 --output {log,stdio} CLI output method
 --log-level {debug,DEBUG,info,INFO,warning,WARNING,error,ERROR,critical,CRITICAL}
 CLI log level
 --server-address SERVER_ADDRESS
 Server address (default: CEPH_NVMEOF_SERVER_ADDRESS
 env variable or 'localhost')
 --server-port SERVER_PORT
 Server port (default: CEPH_NVMEOF_SERVER_PORT env
 variable or '5500')
 --client-key CLIENT_KEY
 Path to the client key file
 --client-cert CLIENT_CERT
 Path to the client certificate file
 --server-cert SERVER_CERT
 Path to the server certificate file
 --verbose Run CLI in verbose mode

Commands:
 {version,gw,spdk_log_level,subsystem,listener,host,connection,namespace,ns,get_subsystems}
 version Get CLI version
 gw Gateway commands
 spdk_log_level SPDK nvmf log level commands
 subsystem Subsystem commands
 listener Listener commands
 host Host commands
 connection Connection commands
 namespace (ns) Namespace commands
 get_subsystems Get subsystems
[root@host01 ~]#
```
2. Create an NVMe subsystem.

The SUBSYSTEM_NQN is a required parameter when creating a subsystem. SUBSYSTEM_NQN is a user-defined string. By default, the gateway appends a group name to the NQN and the subsystem includes the group name. The group name is automatically appended to prevent one or more subsystems from being created with the same NQN in different groups.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 A group name is not appended if the --no-group-append parameter is used when adding the subsystem.

In this example, SUBSYSTEM_NQN is defined as nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1 and `group1` is appended after the subsystem add command. .

**Note:** **Note:** Note:

- The actual created subsystem name is returned with the subsystem add command. Use the returned subsystem name for all subsequent subsystem operations.
- Up to 128 subsystems are supported.

```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port 5500 subsystem add --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN [--serial-number SERIAL_NUMBER] [--max-namespaces MAX_NAMESPACES] [--dhchap-key KEY_VALUE]
```

**Important:** **Note:** Important:
section_path: Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem with nvmeof-cli > Procedure (part 1)

title: Procedure
content:
- NQN and gateway name values must not contain an underscore character.
- Do not use the same NQN for two different gateway groups. Namespaces might not be visible if an initiator is connected to two different gateway groups with the same NQN.

The default --server-port value is 5500.

For extra input, the following parameters can be added to the command:
 
--serial-number
If the serial number is not specified, the number is randomly generated.
 
Input type: String

--max-namespaces
The maximum namespaces per subsystem default is 256.
 
Input type: Number

 --no-group-append
Use this flag to not append a group name to the subsystem NQN.
 
**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 Use this flag with extreme caution. When using this flag, if an initiator is connected to two different gateway groups with the same subsystem NQNs, not all NVMe-oF devices are listed with the nvme list command.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 A group name is not appended to the subsystem NQN only if this option is not used.

Input type: Boolean

--dhchap-key
Use this flag to add a generated DH-HMAC-CHAP key for use with bidirectional in-band authentication.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Use this flag to define in-band authentication during the subsystem creation. The in-band authentication can also be defined later. For more information, see Changing a subsystem authentication key.

Input type: String

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.21 --server-port 5500 subsystem add --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1 --dhchap-key DHHC-1:00:abEcb12F100FNlZkIOkv37idpu/notvalid!!si1VQ09KhKv2g:
Adding subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1: Successful
```
3. Add a listener to define the IP port on the gateway that is to process NVMe/TCP commands and I/O operations.

**Important:** **Note:** Important:

- Listeners must be added to all subsystems for all gateways in the gateway group for High Availability and auto load balancing of namespaces.
- NQN and gateway name values must not contain an underscore character.

```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT listener add --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN --host-name HOST_NAME --traddr GATEWAY_IP
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 listener add --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --host-name host02 --traddr 10.172.19.01
```

To define the IP port on the gateway, be sure to include the --host-name and --traddr parameters.
 For extra input, the following parameters can optionally be added to the command:
 
--trsvcid
Enter the port number. The default port is 4420.
--adrfam
Enter the IP_TYPE. The supported value is IPv4 and the input can be written as either ipv4 or IPV4.
--server-port
Enter the SERVER_PORT number. The default port is 5500.
4. Get the host NVMe Qualified Name (NQN) for each host.

For Red Hat Enterprise Linux initiators

```bash
cat /etc/nvme/hostnqn
```

 For example,
 

title: Procedure
content:
To define block devices and add namespaces on existing rbd images in a Ceph cluster, start directly with step 3.
1. Create an `rbd` pool.

```bash
ceph osd pool create POOL_NAME PG_NUM
 
ceph osd pool application enable POOL_NAME rbd
rbd pool init -p POOL_NAME
```

For example,
 
```
[root@rbd-client ~]# ceph osd pool create pool1
[root@rbd-client ~]# ceph osd pool application enable pool1 rbd
[root@rbd-client ~]# rbd pool init -p pool1
```
2. **Optional: **
Create an image within any RADOS Block Device (RBD) application-enabled pool.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 An image can be created separately, by using this step, or while adding a namespace. To create an image directly during the namespace creation, skip this step and go to step 3. Be sure to add the --rbd-create-image and --size parameters.

```bash
rbd create IMAGE_NAME --size MEGABYTES --pool POOL_NAME
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# rbd create image1 --size 1024 --pool pool1
```

For more information about creating an image, see Creating images.
3. Add a namespace to any subsystem that was created in Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem with nvmeof-cli.
To create an image within an RBD application-enabled pool, use the --rbd-create-image and --size parameters.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Create an image within an RBD application-enabled pool when step 2 was skipped.

Automatic load-balancing makes sure that each namespace receives an assigned load-balancing group. For more information about load balancing, see Using load balancing with scale-up and scale-down with nvmeof-cli.

During a namespace addition, a load-balancing group is automatically assigned to the NVMe-oF namespace with any available NVMe-oF gateway load-balancing group.

It is recommended to allow the NVMe-oF gateway to set the active gateway automatically, and not to force the namespace. The gateway load-balancing group ID of a gateway can be retrieved at any time by running the gw info command. For example:
 
```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP gw info
```

```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT namespace add --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN --rbd-pool RBD_POOL --rbd-image RBD_IMAGE
```

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 The image size can be expanded at any time. For more information see, Expanding a block device image with nvmeof-cli.

- Example of adding a namespace to a block device with a previously created image.
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 namespace add --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --rbd-pool pool1 --rbd-image image1
```
- Example of creating an image and adding a namespace within the same command.
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 namespace add --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --rbd-pool pool1 --rbd-create-image --rbd-image image1 --size 1024
```

title: Managing subsystems with nvmeof-cli
content: As a system administrator, you can add, list, and delete NVMe-oF subsystems by using the command-line interface (CLI).
section_path: Managing subsystems with nvmeof-cli

title: Before you begin
content: Managing NVMe-oF subsystems with the CLI requires the `nvmeof-cli` alias setup. For more information about defining the alias, see step 1 of Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem with nvmeof-cli.
section_path: Managing subsystems with nvmeof-cli > Before you begin

title: About this task
content:
At any point, you can use the -h or --help parameters for command help.
 The following parameters are interchangeable:
 
- --subsystem and -n
- --serial-number and -s
- --max-namespaces and -m
- --dhchap-key and -k

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Creating subsystems with the same NQNs within more than one gateway group causes issues with the NVMe-oF initiators.

Use the commands listed here to manage your subsystems.
 
- Adding a subsystem
- Changing a subsystem authentication key
- Listing subsystems
- Deleting a subsystem

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 The commands here show the SUBSYSTEM_NQN with the subsystem NQN and group name, assuming that the --no-group-append was not added when adding the subsystem. For more information, see Managing subsystems with nvmeof-cli.
section_path: Managing subsystems with nvmeof-cli > About this task

title: Adding a subsystem
content:
Use the subsystem add command to add an NVMe-oF subsystem.
 
```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT subsystem add --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN [--serial-number SERIAL_NUMBER] [--max-namespaces MAX_NAMESPACES] [--dhchap-key KEY_VALUE]
```

The SUBSYSTEM_NQN is a user-defined string with and appended group name, assuming that the --no-group-append was not added when adding the subsystem. In this example it is defined as nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1.
 
**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 Use this flag with extreme caution. When using this flag, if an initiator is connected to two different gateway groups with the same subsystem NQNs, not all NVMe-oF devices are listed with the nvme list command.

**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 NQN and gateway name values must not contain an underscore character.

The default --server-port value is 5500.

The following parameters can optionally be added to the command:
 
--serial-number
If the serial number is not specified, the number is randomly generated.
 
Input type: String

--max-namespaces
The maximum number of namespaces per subsystem default is 256.
 
Input type: Number

--dhchap-key
Use this flag to add a generated DH-HMAC-CHAP key for use with bidirectional in-band authentication.
 
Input type: String

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.0.195.226 --server-port 5500 subsystem add --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --serial-number 1 --dhchap-key DHHC-1:00:abEcb12F100FNlZkIOkv37idpu/notvalid!!si1VQ09KhKv2g:
Adding subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1: Successful
```
section_path: Managing subsystems with nvmeof-cli > Adding a subsystem

title: Changing a subsystem authentication key
content:
Use the subsystem change_key command to change the in-band authentication keys for a subsystem.
 
**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 Using the subsystem change_key command without adding the --dhchap-key parameter removes the existing key.

```bash
subsystem change_key --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN --dhchap-key KEY_VALUE
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli subsystem change_key --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --dhchap-key DHHC-1:00:abEcb12F100FNlZkIOkv37idpu/notvalid!!si1VQ09KhKv2g:
```
section_path: Managing subsystems with nvmeof-cli > Changing a subsystem authentication key

title: Listing subsystems
content:
Use the subsystem list command to list NVMe-oF subsystems associated with a specific gateway.
 
```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT subsystem list [--subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN] [--serial-number SERIAL_NUMBER]
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 subsystem list
Subsystems:
Subtype| NQN | HA State | Serial | Controller IDs | Namespace | Max
 | | | Number | | Count | Namespaces
=============================================================================================================
NVMe | nqn.2016-06.10.spdk:cnode1.group1 | enabled | Ceph1230985676540 | 4081-6120 | 32 | 256 
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NVMe | nqn.2016-06.10.spdk:cnode2.group1 | enabled | Ceph5400985676123 | 4081-6120 | 32 | 256
```
section_path: Managing subsystems with nvmeof-cli > Listing subsystems

title: Deleting a subsystem
content:
Use the subsystem del command to delete NVMe-oF subsystems associated with a specific gateway.
 
```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT subsystem del --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN [--force]
```

Use the --force parameter to delete any existing subsystem namespaces before deleting the subsystem.
 
**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 The --force parameter is optional but if not set and the subsystem contains a namespace, the subsystem deletion results in failure.

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.0.195.226 --server-port 5500 subsystem del --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --force
```

title: Adding a host
content:
Use the host add command to add host access to an NVMe-oF subsystem.
 
```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT host add --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN --host-nqn HOST01_NQN [--dhchap-key KEY_VALUE]
```

**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 NQN and gateway name values must not contain an underscore character.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Specific hosts can be selected, as in the following example. To specify all hosts, use `--host-nqn "*"`.

**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 Only use the --dhchap-key parameter with a single specific host NQN. Do not use `--host-nqn "*"`.

The following is an example of adding NVMe initiator the `nqn.2014-08.org.nvmexpress:uuid:950ddadf-f995-47b7-9416-b9bb233f66e3` host:
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 host add --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --host-nqn nqn.2014-08.org.nvmexpress:uuid:950ddadf-f995-47b7-9416-b9bb233f66e3 --dhchap-key DHHC-1:00:abEcb12F100FNlZkIOkv37idpu/notvalid!!si1VQ09KhKv2g:
```

The following is an example of adding all NVMe initiator hosts:
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 host add --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --host-nqn “*”
```

Only one subsystem can be specified at a time. To specify multiple specific hosts, separate them by using a space.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Do not use commas between host NQNs or quotes (") around the multiple host NQNs. Use the following example format:
 
--host-nqn HOST01_NQN HOST02_NQN

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 host add --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --host-nqn nqn.2014-08.org.nvmexpress:uuid:950ddadf-f995-47b7-9416-b9bb233f66e3 nqn.2014-08.org.nvmexpress:uuid:123ddadf-f456-47b7-9416-b9bb233f67f4
```

title: Adding a listener
content:
Starting from IBM Storage Ceph 8.1, you can add listeners for any of the gateways through any of the gateways in the gateway group. Adding listeners through a gateway group is useful in cases that you plan to add more gateways to a gateway group but the new gateways are still not up and running. It is sufficient to know what the IP address of the new gateways will be and then add the listeners to the IP address. This way, when the gateway joins the group, the gateway automatically begins participating in I/O activity.

 Use the listener add command to add a listener to an NVMe-oF subsystem.
 
```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT listener add --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN --host-name HOST_NAME --traddr GATEWAY_IP
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 listener add --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --host-name host02 --traddr 10.172.19.01
```

Add a listener for each NVMe-oF gateway.

To define the IP port on the gateway, be sure to include the --host-name and --traddr parameters.

The following parameters can optionally be added to the command:
 
--trsvcid
Enter the port number. The default port is 4420.
--adrfam
Enter the IP_TYPE. The supported value is IPv4 and the input can be written as either ipv4 or IPV4.
--server-port
Enter the SERVER_PORT number. The default port is 5500.

content: As a system administrator, you can manage NVMe-oF subsystem namespaces by using the command-line interface (CLI). Use this information to add, delete, resize, and list namespaces. You can also get I/O statistics, change load-balancing groups, and set Quality of Service (QoS) limits for namespaces.
section_path: Managing namespaces with nvmeof-cli

title: Before you begin
content:
Use this information to manage namespaces with no masking. To manage masked namespaces, use the commands that are detailed in Managing masked namespaces with nvmeof-cli.

Managing NVMe-oF subsystem namespaces with the CLI requires the `nvmeof-cli` alias setup. For more information about defining the alias, see step 1 of Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem with nvmeof-cli.
section_path: Managing namespaces with nvmeof-cli > Before you begin

title: About this task
content:
Namespaces are automatically load balanced across gateways in a gateway group during namespace addition and namespace deletion. For more information about load balancing, see Using load balancing with scale-up and scale-down with nvmeof-cli.

At any point, you can use the -h or --help parameters for command help.

The following parameters are interchangeable:
 
- --subsystem and -n
- --uuid and -u
- --rbd-pool and -p
- --rbd-image and -i
- --rbd-create-image and -c
- --block-size and -s

**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 Namespaces might not be visible if an initiator is connected to two different gateway groups with the same NQN.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 The commands here show the SUBSYSTEM_NQN with the subsystem NQN and group name, assuming that the --no-group-append was not added when adding the subsystem. For more information, see Managing subsystems with nvmeof-cli.
section_path: Managing namespaces with nvmeof-cli > About this task

title: Adding a namespace
content:
Use the namespace add command to add a namespace to an NVMe-oF subsystem.
 
```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT namespace add --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN --rbd-pool POOL_NAME --rbd-image IMAGE_NAME
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 namespace add --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --rbd-pool pool1 --rbd-image image1
```

You can optionally add the following parameters to the command:
 
--uuid
Enter the namespace UUID. When multiple namespaces exist on the same subsystem, each namespace has its own UUID.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 When this parameter is not used, the gateway automatically generates a UUID value.

--nsid
Enter the namespace ID of the subsystem.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 When this parameter is not used, the gateway automatically generates an NSID value, the next available value on the subsystem, starting with `1`.

--block-size
Enter the namespace block size.
--size
The size is indicated in bytes, by default. To indicate a different size type, specify the unit. The supported size units are: KB, KiB, MB, MiB, GB, GiB, TB, and TiB.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 The --size parameter can only be used together with the --rbd-create-image parameter.

--rbd-create-image
Create an image within any RADOS Block Device (RBD) application-enabled pool.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 The --size parameter must be used together with --rbd-create-image.

--force
Use the --force parameter to create a namespace even if its image is already used by another namespace.
--rbd-trash-image-on-delete
Instructs the gateway to automatically delete the Ceph Block Device (RBD) image that is created for the namespace when the namespace is deleted.
 This parameter only applies to RBD images created when adding a namespace. If the namespace was added by using an existing RBD image, this image will not be deleted with the namespace.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 The --rbd-trash-image-on-delete parameter can only be used together with the --rbd-create-image parameter.

--no-auto-visible
Makes the namespace visible only to specific hosts. For more information and instructions, see Managing masked namespaces with nvmeof-cli.
--read-only
Use to create a namespace that cannot be modified. Use read-only namespaces to prevent namespace changes during operations such as during disaster recovery tests. The Read-Only or Read-Write status can be seen in the namespace list output.
 
**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 Once a namespace is flagged as read-only it cannot be modified to read-write.

title: Examples
content:
- Add a namespace while creating a Ceph Block Device (RBD) image and pool, while setting the image to automatically delete during the namespace deletion.
 

title: Changing the Ceph Block Device image delete policy for during a namespace deletion
content:
If the Ceph Block Device (RBD) image was set to delete with a namespace, use the command namespace set_rbd_trash_image to keep it after the namespace deletion. Use this command to change an image that was created by using the --rbd-create-image parameter during the namespace creation.

title: Changing namespace visibility
content:
Namespace automatic visibility allows all hosts to view the namespace. To have a namespace be visible to all hosts, use the `auto-visible yes` option. To mask a namespace, for a namespace to only be visible to specific hosts, use the `auto-visible no` option.
 
**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 When namespace masking is enabled, and is changed from `auto-visible yes` to `auto-visible no` the command fails when there are previously connected hosts to the namespace unless the --force parameter is used.

Use the namespace change_visibility command to enable or disable namespace masking on a namespace.
 
```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT namespace change_visibility --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN --nsid NSID --auto-visible <yes|no> [--force]
```

Use no to enable namespace masking and yes to remove namespace masking.

Example for enabling namespace masking

```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 namespace change_visibility --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --nsid 3 –-auto-visible no
```

Example for removing namespace masking

```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 namespace change_visibility --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --nsid 3 –-auto-visible yes --force
```

title: Using load balancing with scale-up and scale-down with nvmeof-cli
content: Namespaces are automatically redistributed across the gateways during scale-up and scale-down processes. This redistribution helps ensure that the load across all gateways in the group are the same. The automatic redistribution process begins automatically after a scale-up or scale-down operation. Use this information to understand how to use and prepare for load balancing with scale-up and scale-down operations.
section_path: Using load balancing with scale-up and scale-down with nvmeof-cli

title: About this task
content:
Adding gateway nodes to a gateway group, also known as scale-up operations, require certain steps before and after the scale-up operation. These steps include:
 
1. Preparing new gateways with listeners defined for each system.
2. Verifying that the new gateway IP addresses are discovered as expected.
3. Reconnecting from the initiators to the subsystems.

The following procedure provides detailed load balancing scale-up steps.

Removing gateway nodes from a gateway group, also known as scale-down operations does not require extra steps. After scale-down, the system automatically failovers the namespaces that correspond to the load balancing group ID of the gateway that is being removed. The namespaces failover to one of the other gateways that remain in the group.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 When running scale-down operations, delete listeners from the deleted gateways for all related subsystems. Deleting listeners is required for scale-down operations but not for gateway node replacement procedures. For more information about deleting listeners, see Deleting listeners.

The first step of the failover verifies that I/O can continue to the remaining namespaces, leaving one of the gateways with more load than the others. Therefore, the system begins a background process will automatically rebalance the namespaces across the existing gateways.

**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 mTLS certificates must include all IP addresses of each of the Ceph NVMe-oF gateways. When adding or removing gateways, if the certificates added during mTLS configuration need to be re-created to include all IP addresses. For more information, see Configuring mTLS authentication.

 Use the following information during scale-up and scale-down, based on your deployment method:
 
- Managing NVMe-oF gateway host labels
- Managing gateways with a specification file
section_path: Using load balancing with scale-up and scale-down with nvmeof-cli > About this task

title: Procedure
content:
Run the following steps before and after the scale-up operations, as indicated.
1. Before adding new gateways to a gateway group, add a listener to define the IP port on the gateway that is to process NVMe/TCP commands and I/O operations.
Repeat this step for all subsystems present in the High Availability gateway group.
 
**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 NQN and gateway name values must not contain an underscore character.

```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT listener add --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN --host-name HOST_NAME --traddr GATEWAY_IP
```

To define the IP port on the gateway, be sure to include the --host-name and --traddr parameters.

For extra input, the following parameters can optionally be added to the command:
 
--trsvcid
Enter the port number. The default port is 4420.
--adrfam
Enter the IP_TYPE. The supported value is IPv4 and the input can be written as either ipv4 or IPV4.
--server-port
Enter the SERVER_PORT number. The default port is 5500.

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 listener add --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --host-name host02 --traddr 10.172.19.01
```
2. Add any required gateway nodes from the gateway group.
For more information, see Managing gateways with a specification file.
3. **Optional: **
Verify that the scale-up operation is complete.

```bash
ceph nvme-gw show NVME-OF_POOL_NAME GW_GROUP
```

Check the following output:
 
- The num-namespaces output of each gateway in `Created Gateways` is of similar value, within just a few numbers of each other.
- The total of each gateway num-namespaces output in `Created Gateways` equals to the total num-namespaces.
- The gateways within the `Created Gateways` equals the number of gateways after the scale-out.

The following example has a total of three gateways with the `Created Gateways` num-namespaces with output of 315, 315, and 314, with a total of "num-namespaces": 944. The rebalance_ana_group, num gws and number of gateways within `Created Gateways` all equal 3 and all gateways are in an AVAILABLE state.

For example,
 
```

 },
```

**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 Continue with the following steps only after the scale-up operation is complete.
4. Run the nvme discover command to verify that the new gateway IP addresses are discovered as expected.
Run this command for each initiator.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 This step is only applicable to RHEL initiators. For ESXi initiators, skip to step 5.

```bash
nvme discover -t tcp -a GATEWAY_IP -s 8009
```

The output provides the IP address (`traddr`) of the new NVMe-oF gateway for the subsystems added with listeners in step 1, which can be connected from this initiator.

Reconnecting Red Hat Enterprise Linux initiators

Use the nvme connect-all command to connect to all gateways in the group, establishing multipath connections.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 When using bidirectional in-band authentication, use the nvme connect command instead of nvme connect-all. The nvme connect command must be run on each gateway for all namespaces to be visible.
 To connect to a specific subsystem, use the following values from the previous step:
 
- subnqn value as the SUBSYSTEM_NQN
- The trsvcid port value

```bash
nvme connect --traddr GATEWAY_IP --transport tcp --nqn SUBSYSTEM_NQN --trsvcid PORT
```

**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 Namespaces might not be visible if an initiator is connected to two different gateway groups with the same NQN.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 Adding the `-l` flag enables the initiator to retry connecting to the gateway in cases where the gateway becomes temporarily unavailable.

```bash
nvme connect-all --traddr GATEWAY_IP --transport tcp -l 1800 -s 8009
```

For example,

 In this example, the `-l` flag is set to retry after 1800 seconds, if the first connection does not succeed.


**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 In cases that a specific connection is required without discovering all of the available gateways, run the nvme fabrics connect command.
 
```bash
esxcli nvme fabrics connect -a NVME_TCP_ADAPTER -i GATEWAY_IP -s SUBSYSTEM_NQN -p 8009
```

section_path: Removing the NVMe-oF service with nvmeof-cli > Before you begin

title: About this task
content:
The following are the three main steps to remove the NVMe-oF service:
 
1. Disconnect the NVMe-oF gateway initiator.
2. Remove the NVMe-oF gateway target.
3. Remove the NVMe-oF service.
section_path: Removing the NVMe-oF service with nvmeof-cli > About this task

title: Procedure
content:
1. Disconnect the NVMe-oF initiator from NVMe-oF target.

Red Hat Enterprise Linux

```bash
nvme disconnect-all
```

VMware ESX initiator 

```bash
esxcli nvme fabrics disconnect -n CONTROLLER_NUMBER -a ADAPTER -s SUBSYSTEM_NQN
```

 Replace the CONTROLLER_NUMBER, NVME_TCP_ADAPTER, and SUBSYSTEM_NQN values with the values retrieved from the esxcli nvme controller list command. The SUBSYSTEM_NQN is listed as `Name` in the system output.
 For example,
 
```
esxcli nvme fabrics disconnect -n 282 -a vmhba64 -s nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode2.group1
```
2. Remove the NVMe-oF Gateway target for each subsystem.

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 The `--force` flag is needed to delete subsystems that contain namespaces.

```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address IP --server-port 5500 subsystem del --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN --force
```

For example,
 
```bash
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 192.0.2.1 --server-port 5500 subsystem del --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --force
```
3. Remove the NVMe-oF service.

1. On the Ceph admin node, remove the NVMe-oF service.

```bash
ceph orch rm nvmeof.NVME-OF_POOL_NAME.GW_GROUP
```

For example,
 
```
[ceph: root@host01 /]# ceph orch rm nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1
```
2. Check that the mon_allow_pool_delete parameter is set to `true`

```bash
ceph config set mon mon_allow_pool_delete true
```
3. On the Ceph admin node, remove the NVME-OF_POOL created to host NVMe-oF service.

```bash
ceph osd pool rm NVME-OF_POOL_NAME NVME-OF_POOL_NAME --yes-i-really-really-mean-it
```

**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 The pool name (NVME-OF_POOL_NAME) must be used twice in the command to remove the pool.

For example,
 
```
[ceph: root@host01 /]# ceph osd pool rm nvmeof_pool01 nvmeof_pool01 --yes-i-really-really-mean-it
```

title: Configuring Quality of Service with nvmeof-cli
content:
As a storage administrator, configure the Quality of Service (QoS) per namespace to adjust the NVMe-oF gateway usage.

Define the QoS per namespace, by using the namespace set_qos command.
 
**Note:** **Note:** Note:
 The commands here show the SUBSYSTEM_NQN with the subsystem NQN and group name, assuming that the --no-group-append was not added when adding the subsystem. For more information, see Managing subsystems with nvmeof-cli.

```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address SERVER_ADDRESS --server-port 5500 namespace set_qos --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN [--nsid NAMESPACE_NSID |--uuid NAMESPACE_UUID] --OTHER_PARAMETER VALUE
```

 For example,
 
```
nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.8.131.18 --server-port 5500 namespace set_qos --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --nsid 1 --rw-ios-per-second 0
```

Table 1 lists the optional QoS parameters and their values that can be defined.

| Parameter name | Value | Notes |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| --uuid | Namespace UUID | Note: Specify either the UUID or NSID. One of the parameters must be specified. |
| --nsid | Namespace NSID | Note: Specify either the UUID or NSID. One of the parameters must be specified. |
| --rw-ios-per-second | RW_IOS_PER_SECOND | Number of allowed read-write I/Os per second. Use 0 for unlimited I/Os. Note: Input values are rounded up to the nearest 1000. |
| --rw-megabytes-per-second | RW_MEGABYTES_PER_SECOND | Number of allowed read-write megabytes per second. Use 0 for unlimited megabytes. |
| --r-megabytes-per-second | R_MEGABYTES_PER_SECOND | Number of allowed read megabytes per second. Use 0 for unlimited megabytes. |
| --w-megabytes-per-second | W_MEGABYTES_PER_SECOND | Number of allowed write megabytes per second. Use 0 for unlimited megabytes. |

title: Managing SPDK logs with nvmeof-cli
content: Get, set, and disable Storage Performance Development Kit (SPDK) log information for NVMe-oF by using the command-line interface (CLI).
section_path: Managing SPDK logs with nvmeof-cli

title: Before you begin
content: Managing NVMe-oF subsystems with the CLI requires the `nvmeof-cli` alias setup. For more information about defining the alias, see step 1 of Defining an NVMe-oF subsystem with nvmeof-cli.
section_path: Managing SPDK logs with nvmeof-cli > Before you begin

title: About this task
content:
At any point, you can use the -h or --help parameters for command help.
 The following parameters are interchangeable:
 
- --level and -l
- --print and -p

**Important:** **Note:** Important:
 When using the optional --format and --output parameters, they must come before the spdk_log_level set command input. For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 --format json --output stdio spdk_log_level get
```

For more information about nvme-of cli command line options, see Using the nvmeof-cli utility for configuring and managing NVMe-oF gateways.

Use the commands listed here to manage your SPDK logs.
 
- Getting the SPDK log level
- Setting the SPDK log level
- Disabling SPDK log flags
section_path: Managing SPDK logs with nvmeof-cli > About this task

title: Getting the SPDK log level
content:
Use the spdk_log_level get command to retrieve the SPDK version.
 
```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT spdk_log_level get
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 spdk_log_level get
```
section_path: Managing SPDK logs with nvmeof-cli > Getting the SPDK log level

title: Setting the SPDK log level
content:
Use the spdk_log_level set command to set the log level for the SPDK output and NVMe over Fabrics target (`nvmf`) log flags.
 
The available SPDK nvmf log levels and SPDK nvmf print levels are: DEBUG, INFO, NOTICE, WARNING, and ERROR.

```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT spdk_log_level set --level SPDK_NVMF_LOG_LEVEL --print SPDK_NVMF_LOG_PRINT_LEVEL
```

The following example sets both the print and log levels to `ERROR`.
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 spdk_log_level set --level ERROR --print ERROR
```
section_path: Managing SPDK logs with nvmeof-cli > Setting the SPDK log level

title: Disabling SPDK log flags
content:
Use the spdk_log_level disable command to remove the log level for the SPDK output and NVMe over Fabrics target (`nvmf`) log flags.
 
```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port SERVER_PORT spdk_log_level disable
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 spdk_log_level disable
```
section_path: Managing SPDK logs with nvmeof-cli > Disabling SPDK log flags

title: Troubleshooting NVMe-oF gateways
content: Understand how to troubleshoot and learn how to fix the most common errors that are related to Ceph NVMe-oF gateway configuration and operational conditions.
section_path: Troubleshooting NVMe-oF gateways

title: Verifying gateway connectivity
content: If Ceph NVMe-oF gateway is not responding as expected, verify gateway connectivity.
section_path: Troubleshooting NVMe-oF gateways > Verifying gateway connectivity

title: Procedure
content:
1. List the NVMe-oF block devices.

```bash
nvme list
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvme list
Node Generic SN Model Namespace Usage Format FW Rev
--------------------- ---------------- ------------------- ----------------------- --------- -------------------------- ---------------- --------
/home/nvme01_node01 /home/ng1n1 SPDK00000000000001 SPDK bdev Controller 1 10,49 MB / 10,49 MB 4 KiB + 0 B 23.01
...
```
2. Verify that the initiator is connected to all NVMe-oF gateways and subsystems in the gateway group.

```bash
nvme list-subsys
```

For example,
 
```
[root@init-nvme-vm5 ~]# nvme list-subsys
nvme-subsys5 - NQN=nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode2
\
+- nvme5 tcp traddr=10.243.64.5,trsvcid=4420 live
+- nvme6 tcp traddr=10.243.64.10,trsvcid=4420 live
+- nvme7 tcp traddr=10.243.64.11,trsvcid=4420 live
+- nvme8 tcp traddr=10.243.64.12,trsvcid=4420 live
nvme-subsys1 - NQN=nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 
\
+- nvme1 tcp traddr=10.243.64.5,trsvcid=4420 live
```
3. Create a filesystem on the target of your choosing. 
Use the target path that was found in step 1.
 
```bash
mkfs NVME_NODE_PATH
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# mkfs /home/nvme01_node01
mke2fs 1.46.5 (20-Dec-2023)
Discarding device blocks: done
Creating filesystem with 2560 4k blocks and 2560 inodes

Allocating group tables: done
Writing inode tables: done
Writing superblocks and filesystem accounting information: done
```
4. Mount the NVMe node on the NVMe-oF directory.

1. Mount NVMe-oF.

```bash
mkdir /mnt/nvmeof
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# mkdir /mnt/nvmeof
```
2. Mount the node on within the NVMe-oF directory.

```bash
mount NVME_NODE_PATH /mnt/nvmeof
```

For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# mount /home/nvme01_node01 /mnt/nvmeof
```
5. Using sudo commands, list mounted NVMe-oF files.

```bash
ls /mnt/nvmeof
```

For example,
 
```
$ ls /mnt/nvmeof
lost+found
```
6. Create a text file within the mnt/nvmeof directory.
For example,
 
```
$ sudo bash -c "echo Hello NVMe-oF > /mnt/nvmeof/hello.txt"
```
7. Verify that the text file can now be reached.
For example,
 
```
$ cat /mnt/nvmeof/hello.txt
Hello NVMe-oF
```

title: About this task
content: When updating the NVMe-oF service specification file changes are stored correctly but they do not immediately reflect inside the running container’s configuration (`nvme_conf`). The updated spec is applied at the orchestration level, but the NVMe-oF service itself does not restart to pick up the new values. As a result, manual redeployment is required to propagate these changes to the container.
section_path: Troubleshooting NVMe-oF gateways > About this task

title: Procedure
content:
1. Ensure that the specification file is properly deployed, by using the ceph orch apply command.
2. Manually redeploy the NVMe-oF service.

```bash
ceph orch redeploy nvmeof.POOL_NAME.GROUP_NAME
```
section_path: Troubleshooting NVMe-oF gateways > Procedure

title: Finding a host NQN
content: A host NVMe Qualified Name (NQN) is a unique identifier The NQN identifies a host system by using FC-NVMe connections, allowing the storage system to recognize and interact with the host.

title: Troubleshooting migration abort command issues
content: If watchers were not removed before running the migration abort command, the process fails
section_path: Resolving FC to NVMe migration issues > Troubleshooting migration abort command issues

title: About this task
content:
Aborting the migration deletes the target Ceph Block Device image. As a result, the abort process fails if the target device is still mounted on the host, as watchers are still present on the Ceph Block Device (RBD) image.

If the target device is still mounted on the host, use the following steps and then retry stopping the migration process, removing the watchers from the Ceph Block Device image.
section_path: Resolving FC to NVMe migration issues > About this task

title: Procedure
content:
1. Unmount the target device.
2. Get the namespace ID (NSID).

```bash
ceph nvmeof namespace list --nqn=NQN
```
3. Delete the namespace.

```bash
nvmeof-cli --server-address GATEWAY_IP --server-port 5500 namespace del --subsystem SUBSYSTEM_NQN --nsid NSID
```

 For more information, see Deleting a namespace within Ceph NVMe-oF gateway > Configuring the NVMe-oF gateway target > Managing namespaces. 
For example,
 
```
[root@host01 ~]# nvmeof-cli --server-address 10.172.19.01 --server-port 5500 namespace del --subsystem nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1.group1 --nsid 1
Deleting namespace 1 from nqn.2016-06.io.spdk:cnode1: Successful
```

title: What to do next
content: Retry stopping the migration. For more information, see Manually migrating FC to NVMe.
